topics: MSA exceptions and redlines, DPA & data residency, KMS/HSM, SLA targets and credits, Dedicated vs Hosted billing models, Purchase Order flow and procurement gating, security docs (SOC2/ISO), escrow/termination clauses
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — we have Maya and Ethan from Redwood, and Samir, Lara, Priya, Tom from BlueArc. Uh, big agenda is vendor intake: the MSA/DPA, SLA expectations, and how billing will flow into your procurement process.
[00:22] Samir (BlueArc-Procurement): Hi, thanks — we only have about 45 to 50 minutes so appreciate you being concise. Our procurement committee needs to understand our risk posture early. We use a standard redline process.
[00:38] Maya (Redwood): Totally, we'll try to map to your timeline. Ethan, do you want to start with the service model and where the SLAs live?
[00:45] Ethan (Redwood-SE): Yeah sure, quick overview: Redwood offers hosted API and Dedicated reserved capacity; for enterprise we also do Private/VPC installs. The SLA for hosted is typically 99.9% uptime with token-level latency targets, Dedicated can be contractually tighter. For auditability we emit per-route logs and tracing. Note: sometimes the product names get munged in notes — we call it Redwood Dedicated (sometimes transcribed as Redwood Dedicate).
[01:12] Lara (BlueArc-Legal): Can you clarify what you mean by "auditability"? Our legal team requires an audit window and log retention details for at least 2 years, plus exportability to our SIEM. Also need to understand your KMS integration — do you allow customer managed keys?
[01:30] Ethan (Redwood-SE): Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated through our KMS integration; for Hosted we offer an optional KMIP/HSM-backed key option or bring-your-own-key via our KMS proxy. There's some nuance on key scoping for cached KV state and logs, we'll spell that out in the security addendum.
[01:48] Priya (CFO): On billing: do you invoice monthly? Our AP team works net-45; bigger question is committed vs burst billing — we don't want surprise overage spikes.
[02:01] Maya (Redwood): Standard is monthly invoicing; we can support net-30 or net-45 in enterprise contracts. On committed vs burst, we typically propose committed reserved capacity with an overage rate and a burst pool. We'll include a couple of billing models in the pricing sheet — committed, blended, and usage-only.
[02:18] Tom (Platform): From engineering perspective, we need to know how model fallbacks work and whether requests to the hosted API might be routed to a cheaper model variant. Any constraints for PII handling?
[02:29] Ethan: Good call. We have routing policies — you can pin routes to model versions, fallback policies, and region constraints. For PII we support redaction at the edge, optional prefix caching behavior, and per-request flags to disable KV cache. We'll note that in the DPA language.
[02:50] Samir: Okay, on the MSA itself — we gave you our standard procurement boilerplate. High level markers: indemnity cap, limitation of liability, data breach notification timing, and termination assistance. We expect to see comments on those items.
[03:07] Maya: Understood. Quick signal on common asks: indemnity cap tweaks (some customers push to remove broad IP indemnity, move to third-party claims only), audit frequency (we give quarterly agreed-upon audits rather than unlimited), and SLA credits formula — often customers want credits higher than our standard; we can negotiate up to a point.
[03:27] Lara: For audit windows, our security policy says we may request one on-site or remote audit per year and need a 30-day window to schedule.
[03:36] Ethan: We can support yearly audits; on-site might be limited by Private/Dedicated customers. For hosted we offer remote assessments and provide SOC 2 reports. On on-site, for Private installs it's usually possible.
[03:51] Priya: Also need clarity on termination assistance and data return — we typically require a 90-day data escrow and assistance converting logs to our S3 schema.
[04:02] Maya: We can add termination assistance language — common is 30–90 days depending on the package and data volumes. For Hosted, we typically provide data exports for 30 days; Dedicated/Private can be extended contractually. We'll put options in the MSA redline.
[04:18] Tom: One practical note: our security team insists on a KMS key we control for encryption at rest for anything that persists beyond ephemeral KV. Does Redwood require any special hardware?
[04:28] Ethan: No special hardware for Dedicated beyond standard GPU hosts; for BYOK we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSMs for Private installs. There is a small operational window to rotate keys and re-encrypt caches — we'll document the expected downtime or maintenance windows.
[04:47] Speaker 6 (possible transcription mismatch): (inaudible) ... escrow and, uh, indemnity cap you know two percent of ARR?
[04:56] Samir: On indemnity, our counsel usually pushes for a cap tied to fees paid in prior 12 months. Can you support that construct?
[05:05] Maya: We typically cap liability at a multiple of fees (e.g., 6–12 months of fees) for standard MSA; for some customers we have a sliding scale. We'll propose a starting point and note where exceptions may require underwriter or executive sign-off.
[05:22] Lara: Also, DPA specifics: data residency — we operate in EU and US and need EU data to stay in EU. Is Redwood able to guarantee region-based routing?
[05:33] Ethan: Yes, regional routing is supported. For Hosted customers we offer region scoping and will ensure EU tenant routing. For Private you manage the region. We'll include region residency commitments in the DPA and in a routing SLA.
[05:49] Priya: Regarding pricing approval — our procurement gate requires an internal pricing sheet with committed spend and the projected ROI. Who owns the pricing template?
[05:58] Maya: Redwood will send a pricing-sheet (we have a standard "enterprise-pricing-v3.xlsx") showing committed tiers, overage rates, and dedicated pool sizing guidance. Ethan will attach benchmarks to support unit economics.
[06:12] Ethan: I'll include latency p95 numbers per model size and a couple of sample throughput runs — note that quantization and sequence length affect kernel selection and cost, so we'll provide a few scenarios.
[06:25] Tom: Can we get a short performance pact: 95th percentile latency under X ms for the recommended committed instance?
[06:33] Ethan: We'll put numbers but need to align on sequence lengths and payloads. I'll provide a p95 baseline for the 512-token average case and for the 1k token case.
[06:44] Maya: Back to contracts, a few specific legal points your team raised in the redlines: 1) Subprocessing & subcontractors, 2) Escrow of models or source if required, 3) Data deletion SLA. Lara, did we miss anything?
[06:59] Lara: Also IP ownership for customer prompts and outputs — our default requests that customer data and outputs remain customer-owned and any jointly developed models are scoped.
[07:09] Maya: Agreed — standard approach is customer retains data/output ownership; models trained by Redwood on public models are Redwood IP. We'll put a clause for mutually agreed fine-tuning/derivative works.
[07:23] Samir: About procurement flow — if we sign an MSA with exceptions, how do we handle redline approvals? Our committee wants a single version with tracked exceptions and a final sign-off by legal + procurement + finance.
[07:36] Maya: We'll deliver an annotated MSA showing proposed language and a separate exceptions summary table for each clause. That tends to accelerate committee reviews.
[07:45] Priya: On invoicing controls: can invoices be sent to two recipients? Our AP and project finance teams need copies. Also, are POs required before provisioning dedicated capacity?
[07:56] Maya: We can send invoices to multiple emails. For Dedicated, most customers issue a PO before provisioning for committed capacity — we can also provision on a trial basis with a SOC 2 + security questionnaire completed.
[08:09] Tom: Security docs — do you have an SSP and a runbook for incident response?
[08:15] Ethan: Yes, we have an SSP, SOC 2 Type II report, and an incident response playbook. We'll share a redacted SSP and the SOC 2 report under NDA. Shared: Security packet link (Redwood_Security_Packet_v2.pdf).
[08:30] Lara: On breach notification timing — we require notification within 72 hours of detection for critical incidents. Is that acceptable?
[08:36] Maya: We usually commit to 72 hours for root-cause and initial notification; full forensics can take longer. We'll include that language.
[08:46] Samir: One more thing — our procurement wants to know about insurance: limits for cyber insurance and whether Redwood carries tech E&O and cyber liability.
[08:55] Ethan: We carry cyber and E&O; we'll confirm current limits and share certificate of insurance.
[09:02] Speaker 6: (mumble) ... discounts for multi-year commit?
[09:05] Maya: Yes, multi-year committed contracts typically have a discount ladder; we will outline year-over-year pricing reductions for 1- and 3-year commits in the pricing sheet.
[09:16] Priya: If we do a 3-year committed Dedicated pool, can we require uptime credit at a higher SLA?
[09:23] Maya: Yes, contractual SLAs can be elevated for committed contracts; we'll surface options and the credit math.
[09:31] Tom: A question about backups and logs — how long are logs retained by default and what's the export process?
[09:38] Ethan: Default retention is 90 days for request logs; we can extend retention for Dedicated/Private. Export is via S3 export job or API. We'll document retention options.
[09:50] Lara: DPA item: deletion timing after termination — we asked for 30 days for active deletion and 90 days for backups. Can Redwood commit?
[09:59] Maya: For Hosted standard, 30-day active deletion + 90-day backups is reasonable; we'll add explicit deletion SLA and attestations in the DPA.
[10:10] Samir: Regarding sign-off path: after Redwood sends redlined MSA, we will route to legal then procurement then CFO for spend sign-off — that usually takes 2–3 weeks internally. Do you have any expedited processes?
[10:21] Maya: If you need expedited, we can do a compressed review and set a single stakeholder review meeting. For exceptions requiring exec-level approval, that can add time. We'll aim to meet your 2–3 week window.
[10:33] Ethan: Quick note on model fallbacks and data leakage: we will include data-use restrictions in the DPA; by default no training on customer data unless explicit.
[10:44] Lara: Good. We will also need sample SAML metadata for SSO and a list of supported IdP features.
[10:52] Maya: We'll attach SAML metadata and SSO integration guide (Shared: SSO-setup.pdf).
[10:57] Priya: One administrative thing — what's the contract owner at Redwood? If we need a single point of contact for invoicing disputes.
[11:04] Maya: I'm the AE and will be primary contact; finance@redwood-inference.com is billing contact. We'll also assign an account manager post-sign.
[11:12] Samir: Are there any special procurement conditions for AI that procurement committee flags? For example, model escrow — we raised this earlier.
[11:20] Ethan: Model escrow is unusual but discussable for certain high-risk use cases; it typically requires a third-party escrow and additional cost. We'll note that as an exception item.
[11:31] Lara: On export controls and cross-border data flows — we need language that prevents transfer to disallowed jurisdictions and a process for lawful requests.
[11:40] Maya: We'll include export control language and a notice process for lawful requests.
[11:47] Priya: Final question: what is the time-to-provision for a Dedicated pool once PO is accepted?
[11:53] Ethan: Typically 2–4 weeks for initial capacity depending on GPU type and region; for simple trials it's 3–5 business days. We'll put the timelines in the offering doc.
[12:04] Maya: OK, summarizing next steps: Redwood sends annotated MSA + exceptions table, pricing sheet with committed and burst options, security packet and SAML metadata. BlueArc to confirm DPA residency/KMS needs and internal PO cadence. We'll reconvene for procurement panel.
[12:21] Samir: Sound good. Thanks team.
[12:24] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs. End call.
